cohort: 1467 children (737 delivered by elective cesarean delivery and 730 by spontaneous vaginal delivery) followed up at the age of 4-7 years
finding: Elective cesarean delivery was not associated with metabolic syndrome in early to middle childhood but was associated with central obesity and hypertension, as well as higher levels of total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol, fasting glucose, systolic/diastolic blood pressure, and BMI compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery.
